headline: IRAN CEASEFIRE SENDS GOLD TO $4,110 AND OIL CRASHING 6% — BARRICK AND AEM UP 5%, LUNDIN AND FQML SPIKE 9%
snippet: Gold climbed 1-1.4% to $4,091-$4,110 (near 3-week high, away from 9-month lows) as the US suspended its nearly two-week campaign of strikes against Iran late Friday July 25 without formal announcement and Tehran ended its retaliatory strikes in response. WTI crude plunged over 6% to approximately $83.10/barrel, easing energy-driven inflation fears ahead of the July 29 FOMC meeting. TSX and US equity futures spiked on the ceasefire news; gold mining equities were the standout performers: Agnico Eagle and Barrick Gold each rose more than 5%, while base metal-exposed miners Lundin Mining and First Quantum Minerals surged above 9%. Silver simultaneously rebounded from its 8-month floor. Gold has now recovered from its recent nine-month low near $4,050, with the ceasefire removing the primary near-term macro headwind of inflation persistence driven by Middle East oil-price risk — clearing the path to a potential Fed hold next week that could catalyze the next leg higher.

headline: SILVER BOUNCES FROM 8-MONTH FLOOR ON CEASEFIRE — $58 BASE HOLDS; 70:1 RATIO STILL IMPLIES 14% RERATING vs GOLD
snippet: Silver rebounded from its 8-month low as the US-Iran ceasefire removed the inflation-premium that had suppressed it relative to gold since the Hormuz oil-price spike in early July 2026. Gold simultaneously defended the $4,000 per ounce level on its way to $4,091-$4,110 intraday. The current 70:1 gold-silver ratio remains materially above its modern historical mean of approximately 60:1, implying approximately 14% silver outperformance vs. gold on a ratio normalization alone — before accounting for silver's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces. With the oil-price overhang now reduced and the FOMC meeting on July 29 priced at a 35-38% hike probability heading into the weekend, the ceasefire creates the cleanest dual-catalyst setup silver has seen since early 2026: a Fed hold removes the last near-term headwind while the structural supply deficit remains intact. Silver at $58 now has an unambiguous path back toward the $60-62 range if macro conditions cooperate this week.

headline: FURY GOLD RETURNS TO EAU CLAIRE AFTER 11-DAY WILDFIRE — THREE RIGS BACK DRILLING IN JAMES BAY AT HIGH-GRADE Au ZONE
snippet: Fury Gold Mines Limited announced July 27 that exploration and drilling activities have fully resumed at the Eau Claire gold project in the Eeyou Istchee Territory of the James Bay region in Northern Quebec, following a precautionary suspension that began July 15-16 when a nearby wildfire forced all personnel to evacuate. All employees and contractors have safely returned to site, and the company is resuming operations with the third drill rig that had been mobilized to site just two days before the evacuation. Fury's most recently reported intercept at Eau Claire was 7.0 g/t gold over 21.0 metres, released alongside the third-rig mobilization announcement on July 13. The 11-day interruption halted what had been an accelerating 2026 drill program; with three rigs now back in operation, the program is positioned to deliver results through the rest of Q3 2026. Eau Claire is one of the most active high-grade gold exploration projects in the James Bay region at $4,091 gold.

headline: HOMELAND URANIUM FULLY PERMITTED TO DRILL CROSS BONES IN COLORADO — INAUGURAL PROGRAM READY TO MOBILIZE (TSXV: HLU)
snippet: Homeland Uranium Corp. (TSXV: HLU) announced July 27 that its wholly-owned subsidiary Shift Exploration Inc. is now fully permitted to commence an inaugural drill program at the 100%-owned Cross Bones Uranium Project in Moffat and Rio Blanco Counties, Colorado. The permitting milestone — the result of an approval process advancing since early 2026 — clears the final regulatory hurdle ahead of mobilization. Cross Bones sits in Colorado's historic uranium country, a region that produced uranium through the 1970s-80s and has seen renewed interest as the US Section 232 critical minerals framework creates policy incentives for domestic uranium production. At $86/lb uranium spot (up 20% year-over-year) and with the Section 232 status report still pending in late July, the timing of the permit award positions Homeland to be among the junior uranium explorers advancing toward first-hole milestones in a policy environment increasingly favorable to domestic producers. The project targets uranium mineralization in the same geological corridor as historic Colorado Plateau-type uranium deposits.

headline: FISSION'S DEAL-MAKING GEOLOGIST ROSS McELROY TAKES CEO OF URANIUM BLANK-CHECK COMPANY SHINE MINERALS (TSXV: SMR.H)
snippet: Shine Minerals Corp. (TSXV: SMR.H) announced July 27 the appointment of Ross McElroy as President, CEO and Director, effective immediately. McElroy is best known as the geologist-CEO who led Fission Uranium Corp. (TSXV: FCU) from the triple R uranium discovery at Patterson Lake South in Saskatchewan through a decade of resource growth and ultimately through the company's $1.14 billion acquisition by Paladin Energy in December 2024. After the Fission acquisition, McElroy moved to Apollo Silver Corp. (TSXV: APGO), where he served as President and CEO before stepping down on July 15, 2026 — just 12 days before his Shine Minerals appointment. The .H designation on Shine Minerals' TSXV ticker indicates the company is a capital pool company (CPC), a structure used in Canada for blank-check acquisitions: a CPC raises capital, then completes a Qualifying Transaction to become a regular listed company. McElroy's appointment to a CPC suggests he is positioning Shine Minerals as a vehicle for an acquisition or exploration transaction, most likely in uranium or precious metals given his track record. For investors who followed the Fission story — one of the largest pure uranium exploration success stories of the past decade — McElroy is a high-credibility signal in a junior resource market that often rewards proven discovery teams.

headline: USA RARE EARTH TAPS NEW CEO AS STOCK BREAKS ALL MOVING AVERAGES — CHINA BAN AND LEADERSHIP VACUUM MEET (NYSE: USAR)
snippet: USA Rare Earth Inc. (NYSE: USAR) announced July 26 that Barbara Humpton will retire and Thras Moraitis will become CEO effective October 1, 2026, with Michael Blitzer elected Executive Chairman immediately. The leadership transition arrives at a particularly difficult moment: USA Rare Earth's stock closed at $14.15 on July 24 and has broken below all exponential moving averages, entering a bearish confirmation pattern. The company is also navigating the June 22, 2026 MOFCOM decision by China's Ministry of Commerce that added USA Rare Earth — alongside MP Materials — to China's export control restricted list, prohibiting supply of China-origin feedstocks to either company. This cut USA Rare Earth off from the Chinese rare earth feedstocks that had underpinned its processing economics at its Round Top Heavy Rare Earth Complex in Texas. Moraitis brings credibility from the Serra Verde acquisition strategy and has been advancing the mine-to-magnet vertical integration thesis. The simultaneous MOFCOM ban and CEO transition creates an operational and strategic vacuum at a company that was positioned as the leading alternative to China's near-monopoly on heavy rare earth processing — at precisely the moment when that monopoly is most consequential.

headline: GT RESOURCES LANDS 10-YEAR YUKON COPPER-NICKEL EXPLORATION PERMIT AT ROAD-ACCESSIBLE CANALASK (TSXV: GT)
snippet: GT Resources Inc. (TSXV: GT) announced July 27 the receipt of a Class III Exploration Permit — valid for 10 years — for the Canalask Copper-Nickel Project in the Yukon. The permit, which covers a road-accessible project in one of Canada's most prospective copper-nickel belts, provides the company with a decade-long exploration window to test targets on the property. Road accessibility is a material differentiator for Yukon copper-nickel projects, which frequently face logistics costs that compress project economics at deposit-scale. GT Resources has previously funded drilling at Canalask through a C$1.8 million flow-through private placement. With copper at approximately $6.33/lb on Comex and nickel supply chains facing geopolitical scrutiny following Indonesia's production quota announcements and DRC cobalt dynamics, a 10-year Class III permit in Yukon represents a multi-cycle exploration platform at a time when Western-jurisdiction copper-nickel projects with existing permits command institutional attention.

headline: GOLD-FUTURES SPECS HAVE GONE MIA — YET $4,000 HOLDS: WHAT'S SUPPORTING GOLD WITHOUT THE SPECULATIVE HERD
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis published within the last 72 hours examines a structural anomaly in the gold market: large speculators in gold futures have become 'MIA' (missing in action), aggressively reducing their net long positions to historically low levels — yet gold has continued to hold above $4,000 per ounce rather than breaking down as the traditional correlation would predict. The historical relationship between spec gold-futures positioning and gold price direction has broken down in 2026. The analysis identifies three converging factors supporting gold without speculative help: shifts in central bank reserve management accelerating gold purchases as a dollar-debasement hedge (Q1 2026 saw 244 tonnes in central bank purchases, the highest quarterly total on record); the dramatic de-escalation in Middle Eastern geopolitics now unfolding (Iran ceasefire removing the oil-inflation premium); and a stubbornly robust US macroeconomic backdrop that keeps rate-cut expectations suppressed while simultaneously validating gold as an inflation hedge. The implication for investors: when specs are absent yet gold holds, the subsequent catalyst that re-attracts speculative capital can produce disproportionate price moves — because the speculative overhang that typically caps rallies hasn't been rebuilt yet.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER MINING STOCKS BOUNCE ON CEASEFIRE — SECTOR ENTERS CRITICAL FOMC WEEK WITH RENEWED MOMENTUM
snippet: The gold and silver mining equity sector opened the final week of July 2026 with a strong ceasefire-driven bounce, as the US-Iran pause in hostilities reduced oil-price risk and rekindled expectations for a Federal Reserve hold on July 29. The bounce arrives at a critical juncture: gold equities (GDX) have been trading at historically wide discounts to spot gold despite record corporate margins — the sector discount that has persisted through the entire post-$5,000 ATH correction is now being tested by the convergence of a geopolitical de-escalation catalyst, a potentially dovish Fed meeting on July 29, and Q2 earnings from Agnico Eagle and Kinross (both reporting July 29) expected to deliver record free cash flow. A sector re-rating from current discount levels requires multiple simultaneous catalysts to close the gap between NAV and market price; the July 29 triple-header — ceasefire backdrop, FOMC hold, and senior producer earnings — represents the most concentrated opportunity for that re-rating since the beginning of 2026.

headline: PANORO'S SECOND DRILL RIG ARRIVES AT COTABAMBAS — 15,000m COPPER-GOLD PUSH INTENSIFIES IN PERU (TSXV: PML)
snippet: Panoro Minerals Ltd. (TSXV: PML) announced July 27 that a second drill rig has arrived and drilling is now underway at the Cotabambas Copper, Gold and Silver Project in the Apurimac region of southern Peru, intensifying the company's fully funded 15,000-metre 2026 exploration program. The program — split across 5,000m to extend the South Pit high-grade resource, 5,000m of infill drilling at the North Pit, and 5,000m testing Targets 7 and 13 located 1-3km west of current resources — is designed to build on the company's landmark June 8, 2026 intercept of 317.6 metres at 1.04% CuEq. Cotabambas hosts a 1.0 billion tonne mineral resource containing 12.5 billion pounds of CuEq (or 15.1 million ounces AuEq), making it one of the largest undeveloped copper-gold-silver deposits controlled by a junior mining company. The addition of the second rig doubles Panoro's drilling rate ahead of an expected resource update. At $6.33/lb copper and $4,091 gold, the project economics are deeply attractive for a bulk-tonnage resource of this scale in a Peruvian copper corridor with established infrastructure and operational precedents.
